findings.title: Interpolating before querySupportsSplitting() defeats the $__range no-split guard
findings.body: The new `.map((query) => datasource.applyTemplateVariables(...))` runs before `partition(queries, querySupportsSplitting)` on line 300. `querySupportsSplitting` deliberately excludes queries containing `$__range` (lines 285-287) because the range variable must be resolved against the full, unsplit time range. Since `applyTemplateVariables` substitutes `$__range` with the full-range duration up front, by the time `isQueryWithRangeVariable(query.expr)` is evaluated the token is already gone, so the guard never fires. Queries using `$__range` — previously sent as a single unsplit request — will now be time-split into daily chunks with the full-range duration baked into every sub-query (e.g. `rate(foo[3d])` executed against each 1-day window), and each chunk's lookback extends well outside its own range, returning wrong/inflated results. The range-variable check needs to run against the uninterpolated expr, or `$__range` queries need to be excluded before interpolation is applied.

findings.title: Shard-split queries are now interpolated twice, duplicating ad hoc filters and re-processing interpolated values
findings.body: `runShardSplitQuery` interpolates every target via `datasource.applyTemplateVariables` (line 52), and each shard sub-request is then executed through `runSplitQuery` (line 163), which after this PR interpolates the same targets again (querySplitting.ts:299). The updated test asserting `applyTemplateVariables` is called 5 times (once here plus once per shard group) confirms the double pass. Consequences: (1) `applyTemplateVariables` also injects `request.filters` ad hoc matchers into the stream selector, so with ad hoc filters configured those matchers are appended twice to every selector sent to Loki; (2) any variable replacement value that itself contains a `$`-style token (e.g. `${...}`) will be re-processed and potentially mangled by the second pass. Before this PR each query was interpolated exactly once. Consider interpolating only in one place — e.g. drop the interpolation in `runShardSplitQuery` since `runSplitQuery` now handles it — while noting the shard-values fetch (`fetchLabelValues`) needs the interpolated selector, so the fetch path must still receive an interpolated expr.
